findings.name: No authentication on remote MCP server
findings.evidence:
REQUEST: POST https://api.bowmark.ai/mcp (JSON-RPC tools/list) with NO Authorization header
RESPONSE: HTTP 200
{"result":{"tools":[{"name":"get_library","title":"Check what Bowmark can do for this task","description":"**Use this whenever a task touches a live website.** It answers, definitively and cheaply, whether Bowmark can already DO the thing: look up current prices, check real availability or stock, search a site, get a quote or a fare, drive a configurator, start a booking, or pull anything that onl …[truncated]
findings.spec_reference: Transports §Security: servers SHOULD authenticate all connections. A protected server MUST answer 401 when authorization is required.
findings.notes: tools/list returned 7 tool(s) without any credential.

findings.name: Cleartext HTTP transport (no TLS)
findings.spec_reference: OAuth 2.1 §1.5 / MCP Authorization: auth-bearing traffic MUST use HTTPS (loopback exempt).
findings.notes: Endpoint is https and its certificate validated.

findings.name: 401 without RFC 9728 WWW-Authenticate pointer
findings.evidence:
REQUEST: POST https://api.bowmark.ai/mcp (JSON-RPC tools/list) with NO Authorization header
RESPONSE: HTTP 200
{"result":{"tools":[{"name":"get_library","title":"Check what Bowmark can do for this task","description":"**Use this whenever a task touches a live website.** It answers, definitively and cheaply, whether Bowmark can already DO the thing: look up current prices, check real availability or stock, search a site, get a quote or a fare, drive a configurator, start a booking, or pull anything that onl …[truncated]
findings.spec_reference: MCP Authorization 2025-06-18: on 401 the server MUST return WWW-Authenticate indicating the protected-resource-metadata URL (RFC 9728 §5.1).
findings.notes: No authentication challenge to inspect (HTTP 200 is not an authentication challenge), so the WWW-Authenticate MUST is not triggered (see no-authentication-remote for the real risk).

findings.name: Missing OAuth Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728)
findings.evidence: PRM GET https://api.bowmark.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp -> HTTP 404; PRM GET https://api.bowmark.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource -> HTTP 404; No usable RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata document (tried: https://api.bowmark.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp, https://api.bowmark.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource).; AS metadata GET https://api.bowmark.ai/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server -> HTTP 200
findings.spec_reference: MCP Authorization: servers MUST expose RFC 9728 metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource including authorization_servers. RFC 9728 §3.1 locates it by inserting the well-known suffix before the resource path.
findings.notes: No RFC 9728 metadata document at either the path-inserted or the origin well-known location.

findings.name: Session identifier carried in URL/query string
findings.evidence:
REQUEST: POST https://api.bowmark.ai/mcp (JSON-RPC initialize) with NO Authorization header
RESPONSE: HTTP 200
{"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"tools":{"listChanged":true},"resources":{},"prompts":{}},"serverInfo":{"name":"bowmark","version":"8.142.2","title":"Bowmark","websiteUrl":"https://bowmark.ai","icons":[{"src":"https://bowmark.ai/icon.svg","mimeType":"image/svg+xml","sizes":["any"]}]},"instructions":"Bowmark runs real tasks on live websites and hands back the result.\n\nRE …[truncated]
--- SSE probe ---
REQUEST: GET https://api.bowmark.ai/mcp with NO Authorization header
RESPONSE: HTTP 405
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Method Not Allowed: this MCP server is stateless and offers no server-to-client stream. Send JSON-RPC over POST."}}
findings.spec_reference: OAuth 2.1 §5: tokens MUST NOT appear in URI query. MCP Streamable HTTP moved the session to the Mcp-Session-Id header.
findings.notes: No header session id and no URL-borne session id observed. The server may be stateless (no session at all), in which case this gap cannot apply.

findings.name: Predictable session identifier
findings.spec_reference: MCP Transports §Session Management: session id SHOULD be globally unique and cryptographically secure. Security Best Practices §Session Hijacking: servers MUST use secure, non-deterministic session IDs; avoid predictable/sequential ones.
findings.notes: Server answered initialize but issued no Mcp-Session-Id header, so there is no stateful session identifier to assess. (Protocol-level sessions were removed in MCP 2026-07-28, so this is expected on current servers.)

findings.name: Origin header not validated (DNS rebinding)
findings.evidence:
REQUEST: POST https://api.bowmark.ai/mcp (JSON-RPC initialize) with NO Authorization header Origin: https://evil.attacker.example
RESPONSE: HTTP 200
{"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"tools":{"listChanged":true},"resources":{},"prompts":{}},"serverInfo":{"name":"bowmark","version":"8.142.2","title":"Bowmark","websiteUrl":"https://bowmark.ai","icons":[{"src":"https://bowmark.ai/icon.svg","mimeType":"image/svg+xml","sizes":["any"]}]},"instructions":"Bowmark runs real tasks on live websites and hands back the result.\n\nRE …[truncated]
findings.spec_reference: MCP Transports §Security Warning: servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks.
findings.notes: initialize from forged Origin 'https://evil.attacker.example' succeeded (HTTP 200 with a valid result) — the server accepts cross-origin requests it should reject.

findings.name: CORS reflects arbitrary origin with credentials
findings.evidence: no Access-Control-Allow-Origin in response to Origin https://evil.attacker.example
findings.spec_reference: Not in the MCP spec. General web security: reflecting an arbitrary Origin in Access-Control-Allow-Origin together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true lets any website make credentialed cross-origin calls.
findings.notes: Server grants no cross-origin access (safe; MCP clients aren't browsers).

findings.name: OAuth endpoint not served over HTTPS
findings.spec_reference: OAuth 2.1 §1.5 & MCP Authorization §2.8: all OAuth protocol URLs MUST use https (loopback exempt). RFC 8414 mandates https for issuer / jwks_uri / metadata path.
findings.notes: All 5 discovered OAuth URL(s) use https or loopback.

findings.name: Missing OAuth Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414)
findings.spec_reference: MCP Authorization §2.3.2: clients MUST follow RFC 8414 to obtain AS metadata; authorization servers MUST provide it. Distinct from RFC 9728 PRM (#4).
findings.notes: RFC 8414 Authorization Server Metadata resolved successfully.

findings.name: Implicit grant advertised (forbidden by OAuth 2.1)
findings.spec_reference: OAuth 2.1 §1.8 removes the implicit grant; MCP §2.3 mandates OAuth 2.1. RFC 8414: response_types_supported 'token' or grant_types_supported 'implicit' advertise it.
findings.notes: response_types_supported has no 'token' and no 'implicit' grant advertised — implicit grant not usable.
